name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.12.0: cross-checks PostgreSQL 17 closures, SQL and SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against gold SQL. Three independently authored, fixture-bound expect examples cover raw missing-stock NULL, explicitly normalized zero after filtering, and composite region/label result keys. Opt-in counterexample --constraint-audit compares trusted SQL in two bounded domains: the declared constraint profile and an explicitly relaxed projection, accepting relaxed witnesses only outside the full original profile. A strict versioned manifest binds exact constraints, caller-claimed provenance and selected declarations; separate versioned replay binds each arm and exact inputs. Version 1 shrinks rows only and preserves original finite values, types and row bounds. A declared-domain disagreement fails; outside-domain disagreement and bounded no-witness outcomes are diagnostic not_run, never pass. No equivalence, causal necessity, false constraint or actual production defect is claimed. Existing default behavior and dependency pins are unchanged; the audit does not change operational V1-V5 or report verdicts. Rerun build, reason, cube, verify and report after upgrading. No business correctness, data completeness, shared whole-run snapshot or runtime attestation is claimed.

Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
